claims.text: In single-phase FCC multi-component concentrated alloys, the magnitude of short-range chemical ordering governs strength and deformation behavior.
Slow cooling enhances short-range chemical ordering relative to rapid quenching.
Enhanced short-range chemical ordering creates localized variations in bonding.
Localized bonding variations associated with short-range order act as intermittent obstacles to dislocation motion.
Enhanced short-range chemical ordering increases yield strength.
Enhanced short-range chemical ordering promotes early strain localization.
Rapid quenching can produce a single-phase FCC Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Mn-type alloy with minimal short-range chemical order.
Identical alloy compositions will be compared after rapid quenching and slow cooling while other microstructural factors are held constant.
Atom probe tomography or diffuse scattering can provide quantitative metrics of short-range chemical order.
Chemically ordered clusters modify local energy barriers encountered by moving dislocations.
Dislocations traversing chemically ordered clusters undergo intermittent pinning and unpinning.
Intermittent dislocation pinning and unpinning raises yield strength and produces localized strain concentrations.
Slow-cooled samples with greater short-range order will have higher yield strength than rapidly quenched samples.
Slow-cooled samples with greater short-range order will exhibit earlier strain localization than rapidly quenched samples.
Rapidly quenched samples will exhibit lower yield strength and more homogeneous plastic flow than slow-cooled samples.
The proposed relationship should hold from room temperature through 200–400°C while the alloy remains single-phase FCC and short-range order is the primary varying microstructural feature.
The effects may change outside the stated temperature range or when additional phase transformations occur.

A lack of statistically significant differences in yield strength or strain localization despite clearly different short-range-order levels would falsify the proposed governing role of short-range order.
